categories.main_business_segments: JMDC operates two main business segments: Health Big Data and Telemedicine. The Health Big Data segment includes services for industry clients (such as pharmaceutical and insurance companies), insurers and individuals (including health insurance societies and municipalities), and healthcare providers (such as hospitals and pharmacies). The Telemedicine segment focuses on remote diagnostic imaging services, primarily through its subsidiary Doctor Net.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: JMDC's core technologies revolve around the collection, anonymization, and analysis of large-scale healthcare data, including medical claims (receipts), health checkup data, and member registries. The company leverages proprietary data platforms, advanced analytics, and AI-driven solutions (such as the AI-RAD diagnostic engine) to deliver insights and services. For telemedicine, it utilizes cloud-based matching and ASP systems to connect medical institutions with radiology specialists.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include pharmaceutical companies, insurance companies, health insurance societies, municipalities, hospitals, and other healthcare providers. The company also serves individual health insurance members through its PHR (Personal Health Record) platform, PepUp. Major end markets are the Japanese healthcare, insurance, and pharmaceutical industries, with growing initiatives targeting municipalities and general consumers.
categories.geographic_coverage: JMDC's operations are primarily based in Japan, with nearly all revenue and assets located domestically. However, the company is beginning to explore overseas expansion, particularly in Asia, in partnership with Omron Corporation.
categories.supply_chain_position: JMDC operates downstream in the healthcare data value chain, providing data analytics, consulting, and digital health solutions directly to end users such as insurers, healthcare providers, and pharmaceutical companies. In telemedicine, it acts as a service platform connecting hospitals with specialist doctors.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding the volume and variety of healthcare data, enhancing value-added analytics and consulting services, and developing new digital health solutions such as AI-powered diagnostic tools. R&D focuses on AI for medical imaging, advanced data analytics, and the integration of new data types (e.g., genomics, activity data) into its platforms. The company also emphasizes information security and privacy protection.
categories.revenue_model: JMDC generates revenue primarily through data extraction and analysis services (ad hoc sales), database access licensing (database sales), consulting, application development, and subscription-based digital health services. In telemedicine, revenue comes from remote diagnostic matching services and ASP system usage fees. Additional income is derived from factoring services and device sales (e.g., wearables).
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: JMDC is a leading player in Japan's healthcare big data and telemedicine sectors, with the largest private health data repository and the largest domestic network of radiology specialists for remote diagnostics. Competitors include other healthcare data analytics firms, IT system vendors, and telemedicine providers, but JMDC differentiates itself through data scale, integration, and advanced analytics capabilities.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2025, JMDC reported consolidated revenue of 41.7 billion yen, up 36.5% year-on-year, with EBITDA of 10.9 billion yen and net profit attributable to owners of 7.3 billion yen. The company has demonstrated strong growth, particularly in Health Big Data (up 42.3% YoY), and has expanded its workforce to over 2,100 employees. The balance sheet shows total assets of 143 billion yen and robust cash flow from operations.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: JMDC offers unique value through its comprehensive, anonymized healthcare data platform, advanced analytics, and ability to deliver actionable insights for healthcare cost optimization, disease prevention, and operational efficiency. Its PepUp platform provides personalized health management for individuals, while its telemedicine services address the shortage of radiology specialists. The company emphasizes data security, privacy, and the integration of diverse data sources to create synergistic value for clients.
